messages:
maria: Quick docs question — API ref for /v1/users GET shows `display_name: string` in the response schema but our service returns null for bot/service accounts. Example currently only has a non-null string which is misleading.

ben: I think the API change last quarter made display_name nullable to avoid migrations. PR #4321 updated the schema but not the examples. We should show both cases: non-null string and null, and add a short note in the schema description.

sam: I can update the TypeScript SDK snippet to handle nulls safely. Proposed snippet:
```ts
const displayName = resp.user?.display_name ?? ""
console.log(`name: ${displayName}`)
```

maria: Also add an inline JSON example showing null for clarity:
```json
{
  "user": { "id": "u_123", "display_name": null }
}
```

ben: Add a 1-line migration note: "display_name may be null for legacy or bot accounts; guard accesses with optional chaining or provide a default." Keep it short.

sam: Assign to @ben and @maria. I'll open a small PR to update examples and the TS snippet: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5678

maria: Nice. CI: docs-lint and snippet-check need to run. @ci-bot can you run snippet-check when the PR is ready?

ci-bot: snippet-check passed on branch update/examples-null-displayname — 1 file changed

ben: I'll merge after changelog entry and CI green. Also add a brief note in the API compatibility section.

maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
